steps.description: Implement the rigid and fat family functions as described in the hypothesis, ensuring proper normalization of y/yv to O(1) and maintaining (N,1) shape for all arrays. The rigid family will be a low-dimensional polynomial/trigonometric set that can be uniquely determined by w points, while the fat family will be high-degree random polynomials that cannot be uniquely determined within h≤64. plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The rigid family is defined by a set of linear algebraic constraints that reduce the solution space to a finite-dimensional subspace spanned by orthogonal polynomials, enabling exact interpolation with width-independent capacity. | This hypothesis is most testable: it directly predicts N_c(w) = O(1) for rigid families (flat/decreasing trend) and N_c(w) = ∞ for fat families (unreachable), matching the binary判别 criterion. steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Implement the constrained family generation module with mathematically defined rigid and fat families. The rigid family will use a low-dimensional algebraic constraint manifold (rank-k linear operator on a fixed basis) to ensure unique determination with small width w, while the fat family will use high-dimensional x-dependent polynomial constraints with degrees of freedom >> w to induce heavy-tailed error distributions. Include proper O(1) normalization of constraint outputs and (N,1) array shapes, separate training/held-out data generation with independent noise injection, and implement scale normalization to prevent magnitude-based failure. plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The rigid family forms a linear subspace of dimension $d \le w$ in function space, where the constraint matrix $\Phi_{ij} = \phi_j(x_i)$ has full rank, ensuring a unique interpolant; thus N_c(w) remains bounded by a constant independent of w as the solution space is algebraically constrained.

steps.description: Implement the rigid family as a linear subspace with dimension d = min(w, 5) (saturating at w=5 to test boundedness), using basis functions φ_j(x) = T_{j-1}(x) (Chebyshev polynomials) for j=1,...,d, ensuring the constraint matrix Φ_ij = φ_j(x_i) has full rank. The family returns normalized y/yv values (divided by std) to maintain O(1) magnitude. X/y serves as training constraints and Xv/yv as held-out constraints (non-overlapping points). This tests whether N_c(w) remains bounded by a small finite value (≤8) as w increases, indicating rigidity, with the prediction that violation count will saturate as d reaches 5.

plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The rigid family defines a linear subspace of dimension $d \le w$ in function space, where the constraint matrix $\Phi_{ij} = \phi_j(x_i)$ has full column rank, ensuring a unique solution for coefficients $c$ via $\Phi c = y$. This algebraic structure guarantees that once $w$ constraints are satisfied, the solution is uniquely determined across all test points, explaining the observed flat $N_c(w)$ trend. | pro: Directly explains the bootstrap success with small widths; aligns with the linear algebra interpretation of rigid constraints. con: Requires verifying the rank condition of the constraint matrix; may not capture non-linear interactions in the fat family. |
